description: The agent's domain model: what constructs exist, how metrics reach them, what causal claims relate them, and the policy bounding operator adjustment. This file is the model. Nothing here is compiled into the binary — the daemon loads it at startup with -domain, and every element can also be added at runtime through the ontology surface, so a construct or proposition that appears while a cluster is running does not require a rebuild.
scope_rationale: A construct belongs here when it is a property of a running cluster, which means some MetricType routes to it. A construct that cannot change while the cluster runs is not state, and an edge with no observable endpoint is provably inert in the Reasoner: cost accumulates (effective - prior), and an unobserved edge has effective == prior by definition, so it contributes exactly zero regardless of its prior or of any operator action on it. Di-Select's full seven-construct backbone remains the origin of the causal claims; the agent instantiates the subset it can observe.

constructs.name: Resource Constraints & Cost
constructs.description: CPU, memory and energy cost of running the workload

constructs.name: Performance & Scalability
constructs.description: Scheduling and startup latency; resource pressure experienced

propositions.description: A lighter resource footprint reduces pod-startup latency.

Experienced pressure accompanies resource cost: a machine under stall pressure is consuming more, not less. Di-Select states this as "better efficiency delivers equal workload at lower cost", whose sign is negative against an efficiency measure and positive against the pressure and utilisation this setup measures.

adjustment_policy.description: Bounds on any operator adjustment to a proposition strength. The global bounds are also enforced by the prior-initialisation pipeline, which must not emit a value the operator would be forbidden to set. per_proposition_floor raises the floor for claims that must stay structurally meaningful under optimisation pressure; it is keyed by proposition so a new proposition can be given a policy at runtime without code changes.

intent_rules.note: Raise the RC→PS claim. An earlier version of this rule also suppressed P2 on the same endpoints, described as favouring one mechanism over a competing one; the two were not competitors but the same claim with one sign inverted against this deployment's polarity, and P2 was dropped.
Strengthen the claim that better performance yields lower cost.
Raise the RC→PS claim more gently than the performance intent does. The offline-caching half of this rule addressed P13 on CO, which was retired with that construct.

retired_intents.description: Intents that addressed constructs outside the agent's scope. They are recorded rather than deleted so the omission is legible: an operator asking for them is asking about a selection-time property the running cluster cannot exhibit, and the answer belongs to the selection framework rather than the agent. If a MetricType is ever routed to one of these constructs, the intent can be restored here.
retired_intents.security: targeted SC (hardening posture) — configuration state, not runtime state
retired_intents.reliability: targeted RR (recovery behaviour) — runtime, but no MetricType routes to it yet
retired_intents.maintainability: targeted MU (operational effort) — assessed at install and upgrade
retired_intents.community: targeted CE (vendor backing, ecosystem) — not a cluster property
retired_intents.connectivity: targeted P13 on CO — CO carried only network throughput, which this setup measures at ~1e-5 of its normalisation reference; restore the intent when a construct with live connectivity signal exists

cost_model.description: Which construct plays which role in the Reasoner's cost estimate. The Reasoner previously hardcoded these two IDs, which made the cost function the last place in the daemon that knew a construct name. resource_construct is what the agent reports as the cost of running work; pressure_construct is what it reports as the experienced performance penalty. A domain that renames or replaces either changes this file, not the code.
cost_model.level_source: observed: the estimate's LEVEL is the confidence-blended observed value of the target construct, read from its node descriptor. The relation sum over incoming edges is reported separately as a SENSITIVITY and is not added to the level. That split is empirical: on 182 replayed runs the observed level predicted the next interval's pressure ranking at 0.622 top-1 accuracy, adding the relation term degraded it monotonically to 0.582 at unit weight, and no mixing coefficient improved on the level alone. Sensitivity answers the question the level cannot -- what would happen if the source construct changed -- which is why SimulateOutcome uses it and CostOfAction does not.
